root_cause.summary: bucket_by_page and confidence_by_page (dicts keyed by page id) are populated ONLY from req.metadata.get('bucket') / req.metadata.get('confidence') while replaying each trace. No code path in either evict_value_dataset_v1.py or evict_value_wulver_v1.py ever calls a bucket/confidence-annotation step (grep-verified: zero writes to metadata['bucket']/['confidence'] anywhere in src/lafc/). A working annotation function, attach_perfect_buckets(), exists in src/lafc/predictors/buckets.py, but it was built for a different, separate experiment (atlas_v1 policy comparisons; buckets.py predates evict_value_wulver_v1.py in git history) and was never wired into the evict_value dataset-generation path. As a result bucket_by_page/confidence_by_page are permanently empty dicts for every trace this generator ever processes, so every .get(page, default) call returns the hardcoded default (0 for bucket, 0.5 for confidence) for every row.
evidence: grep -rn "metadata\['bucket'\]\s*=\|metadata\['confidence'\]\s*=" src/lafc/ -> zero matches (confirmed nothing ever writes these keys)

root_cause.classification: RECOVERABLE_GENERATION_BUG at the code level (the missing wiring is a provable, fixable gap), but NOT SCIENTIFICALLY_RECONSTRUCTABLE for this release: the only available bucket-annotation function, attach_perfect_buckets(), derives bucket purely from req.actual_next (perfect future ground truth), which would (a) inject genuine future-information leakage into columns the benchmark otherwise carefully keeps online-computable, and (b) fabricate a 'perfect oracle predictor' and present it as if it were an authentic historical fallible predictor's output -- both explicitly forbidden by this repair's hard rules. No other predictor implementation in the codebase produces a non-oracle, non-fabricated bucket/confidence score for these specific traces (Request.predicted_next defaults to math.inf and is only ever populated by (a) trace files that already embed real external predictions -- not the case for any of this release's five raw traces -- or (b) noisy.py's synthetic noise-injection wrapper, which perturbs actual_next and is itself an experimental construct, not a historical value).
